description: Name evidence and safe storage policy for translation, hack, aftermarket, homebrew, unlicensed, bootleg, prototype, demo, beta and sample game variants. Filename parsing emits candidates only.

filename_policy.original_verified_dump: preserve exact system DAT name; never add variant metadata to that basename
filename_policy.confirmed_complete_variant: keep the base title and a concise translated-language or variant suffix; add patch version/credit only when independently evidenced
filename_policy.unknown_fields: preserve raw filename tags and leave normalized fields null

candidate_rules: T+ and T- tags are translation evidence candidates; they do not prove the patch is applied.
[h], hack, translated, translation, PT-BR, and localized audio labels inside release groups are candidate markers.
Abbreviated language aliases after translated/translation markers, and explicit by-name credits, are retained as candidates only.
Homebrew, unlicensed (Unl), bootleg (Pirate/Bootlet), aftermarket, prototype (Proto/Unreleased), demo, beta, and sample release-group labels are retained as raw candidate categories only.
Multiple release-category markers remain multiple candidates; do not choose a folder or rewrite the name until content identity, integrity, dependencies, and frontend loading are confirmed.
G-, V-, A-, and P- values are preserved as raw release metadata candidates; their roles are not inferred beyond their tag letter.
A matching documentation basename is a reference candidate, not proof that the note describes the exact file bytes.
